headline: Autodesk grows revenue 17% with a 39% operating margin and raises full-year targets, but billings lag at 12%
takeaway: Revenue rose 17% to $2.16 billion (14% in constant currency), with a 39% adjusted operating margin and adjusted EPS of $3.20. Billings grew a slower 12% to $2.07 billion. Full-year guidance now includes MaintainX. The shares fell 3.5% the next day.
results: Revenue was $2.16 billion, up 17% reported and 14% in constant currency. Architecture, engineering and construction, the largest product family, grew 19% to $1.097 billion; AutoCAD brought in $525 million and manufacturing $403 million. Billings rose 12% to $2.07 billion.

The adjusted operating margin reached 39%. GAAP earnings per share were $2.68, including a tax benefit of about $105 million, and adjusted EPS was $3.20. Free cash flow for the quarter was $505 million.
mgmt: Chief executive Andrew Anagnost said that as AI becomes widely available, the edge will come from combining it with trusted engineering tools, project data and industry workflows, which is the strategy Autodesk is executing. Chief financial officer Janesh Moorjani pointed to strength in construction and emerging markets and strong renewal rates, and said the midpoints of full-year targets were raised despite a stronger dollar.

For the fourth quarter Autodesk expects revenue of $2.220 to $2.235 billion and adjusted EPS of $3.21 to $3.26. For the full year it guides to revenue of $8.36 to $8.375 billion, billings of $8.60 to $8.65 billion, adjusted EPS of $12.70 to $12.76 and free cash flow of $2.725 to $2.75 billion, including the MaintainX acquisition.
view: This was a clean quarter on revenue and profit. Growth of 14% in constant currency for a design-software company of this size is strong, and a 39% operating margin shows the new direct-billing model is delivering the efficiency management promised when it was introduced.

The market focused on billings. Growing 12% while revenue grows 17% means less new business is being invoiced than is being recognised, and billings lead revenue for a subscription company. Part of the gap is timing from the transaction-model change and multi-year contracts, but investors paying for durable mid-teens growth want to see the two lines converge, which explains the 3.5% fall to $246.79.

At roughly 19 times this year’s EPS guidance and a free cash flow yield above 5%, Autodesk is priced well below most software peers with similar margins. The bull case is that construction and manufacturing digitise for years and Autodesk keeps taking share; the bear case is that AI design tools lower the barrier to entry and that slower billings are the first sign of it. The valuation already leans cautious.
watch: Whether billings growth recovers toward revenue growth in the fourth quarter, the contribution and integration of MaintainX, and the first guidance for fiscal 2028 in late February.
